assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Separate methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers with boundary values/value sets; max 40% represented.
assertions.evidence: Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40 ... Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40

assertions.text: 30-day rolling window boundary tested: 30 days included, 31 excluded.
assertions.evidence: Exactly 30 days ago is still in window ... 31 days ago has fallen out of the window

assertions.text: 30-day window exercised at time-of-purchase granularity, not whole days only.
assertions.evidence: History rows use daysAgo integers (29,30,31) and converter does PURCHASE_TIME.minusDays(daysAgo) with no hour-level distinction

assertions.text: Value sets in tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount; no cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5 ... Within second tier | {11, 12, 13, 14} | 10

assertions.text: Discount ladder table uses value sets for ticket count column to group counts within same tier.
assertions.evidence: Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0

assertions.text: Tier-to-discount mapping expressed once, not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount repeats ladder values (0,10,40) and calculatesDiscountEndToEnd repeats (0,5,10,20) beyond the dedicated ladder table

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description present, provides context beyond restating rows.
assertions.evidence: "every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window (counting the ticket being purchased now) raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column with a value set showing discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns: Scenario | Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount? — no Zone column

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count
assertions.evidence: Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR}
assertions.evidence: Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table
assertions.evidence: Table only covers 0, 5, 10, 35, 40 - rows for 15, 20, 25, 30 tiers are absent

assertions.text: Each tier expressed as a single row, not split across multiple rows
assertions.evidence: Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5 ... Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5 -- same tier split into two rows

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively
assertions.evidence: [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 15/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 29/SINGLE/ZONE_1] ... 'Exactly 30 days ago is still in window'

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd are separate @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: countSingleTicketsInWindow table has 7 focused rows; discountForCategoryAndTripCount has 5 rows dedicated to category dispatch

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: Discount values vary across rows (0,5,10,35,40; 0,3,1,1,0,3,3; 20,0,10,10,40) so no table returns a constant or trivially copied value throughout

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'every 5th single ticket... raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap' and '30 days' boundary is shown via day-count entries like 30/SINGLE/ZONE_1

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or method name) states what the code under test does
assertions.evidence: void discountForTripCount(...), void countSingleTicketsInWindow(...), void calculatesDiscountEndToEnd(...) name the computed behavior, not a bare domain fact

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: PURCHASE_TIME is only used as a relative anchor (`PURCHASE_TIME.minusDays(daysAgo)`) and TravelerCategory.ADULT in parsePastPurchase doesn't affect the counting outcome per the described rules, so no outcome-affecting constant is hidden.

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "Zone must never affect the count." is backed by rows using ZONE_1, ZONE_2, ZONE_3, e.g. "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3"; and "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20" covers the trips domain via a value set.
